items.text: The FBI's national crime database, which police use to check warrants and run background checks, was apparently breached by hackers, CNN reported Friday night.
items.detail: The FBI is investigating the suspected intrusion into the National Crime Information Center, which federal, state and local agencies use to share warrants, criminal histories and background-check data, according to two people briefed on the probe, CNN reported; Reuters and NBC News carried the report. The FBI did not comment. It would be the second breach of an FBI system in recent months, after a September hack of an FBI jobs website exposed data on employees. Separately, NBC News reported that a U.S. Department of Agriculture system used to pay farmers was hit by a cyberattack this week; USDA has not commented publicly.
items.why: Officers nationwide rely on the database on every traffic stop and arrest, and it follows a week of outages at banks, air traffic control and the NSA.

items.text: Two more tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz were hit by unidentified projectiles off Oman early Saturday, less than an hour apart, the British navy's UKMTO center said.
items.detail: The first tanker was struck on its stern about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, at about 0500 GMT (midnight ET); about 50 minutes later a second outbound tanker was hit in its engine room about 17 nautical miles east of Khasab. No one was reported hurt, and any environmental damage was not yet known, UKMTO said. The attacks follow Friday's strike that set a tanker on fire about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab. The ships were not named.
items.why: Strikes on ships in the strait, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war, keep oil prices and the Iran war on edge.

items.text: The Trump administration's overhaul of a $4 billion homelessness program was unlawful, a federal judge ruled Friday, blocking a shift of money away from permanent housing.
items.detail: U.S. District Judge Mary McElroy in Providence, R.I., ruled in a suit by 22 states, the District of Columbia and housing groups that the Department of Housing and Urban Development broke the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act by adding grant criteria for the Continuum of Care program, including a plan to set aside $1.3 billion for transitional housing and services-only grants. She also struck limits on needle-exchange work and a "self-sufficiency" test. HUD must let applicants revise applications until Dec. 1 and award the money by Dec. 31. HUD Secretary Scott Turner said the ruling disrupts funding days before awards and that HUD may appeal. An appeals court had overturned her earlier order on different grounds.
items.why: The program funds housing for homeless veterans, families and people with disabilities in nearly every community.

items.text: The S&P 500 and the Dow both fell into a correction Friday, more than 10% below their record highs, as the AI stock sell-off deepened.
items.detail: By preliminary closing figures, the S&P 500 fell 3.59% to 6,918.45, its seventh straight loss and longest losing streak since February 2020. The Nasdaq dropped 5.13% to 22,654.15 and turned negative for 2026, and the Dow lost 1.85% to 48,188.18. All three had their worst week since April 2025. Nvidia fell about 14% and Micron about 14%; Anthropic's shares posted a steep loss on their second day of trading. Bitcoin dropped below $60,000. Traders are pricing a near-certain quarter-point Fed rate hike in December.
items.why: The slide hits the 401(k)s and retirement savings of tens of millions of Americans, and it came a day after Anthropic's record IPO failed to steady AI shares.

items.text: An Anthropic mathematician, Levent Alpöge, says he and the company's Claude AI found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, math's most famous unsolved problem; experts have not confirmed it.
items.detail: Alpöge posted the proof in the Lean language, which checks each step by computer, and said it covers the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland told Scientific American he compiled the Lean code independently and called it "an historic moment," but said much work remains to understand the proof. The 1859 problem, about the pattern of prime numbers, carries a $1 million Clay Mathematics Institute prize.
items.why: If it holds up, it would be the biggest result in mathematics in generations and was done largely by AI.

items.text: A tanker leaving the Strait of Hormuz caught fire Friday after being hit by an unknown projectile, the British navy's UKMTO center said; no one was hurt.
items.detail: The strike happened about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, at 1500 GMT. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the tanker hit a mine. It is at least the third tanker reported hit near Khasab since Monday. Separately, the Treasury Department sanctioned four Iranian regime insiders it said sell oil for the government, including a former Revolutionary Guards intelligence officer.
items.why: Attacks on ships in the strait, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war, keep fuel prices and the war on edge.

items.text: Russia fired more than 400 drones and about 110 missiles at Ukraine overnight, killing at least eight people, after Putin vowed revenge for strikes on the Crimea bridge.
items.detail: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said 27 of the missiles were ballistic and that the attack targeted energy, railway and logistics sites. Six people died in Kyiv, three of them water-utility workers, and two at a railway station in Lviv. Three bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv were hit, and emergency power cuts hit western Ukraine. Ukraine's air force said it downed 380 drones, 79 cruise missiles and three ballistic missiles.
items.why: It is one of the largest air attacks of the war, a day after the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in China.

items.text: Two Russian missiles and a drone crashed in Poland during Friday's barrage on Ukraine, and NATO's chief visits Warsaw Saturday; Poland called it a deliberate provocation.
items.detail: Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said a Kh-101 cruise missile fell near Nowy Lipowiec, a second object believed to be a missile near Rudnik nad Sanem and a jet-powered drone near Mołodycz, all in southeastern Poland. No one was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the objects were certainly Russian and the timing, during a British- and French-led Coalition of the Willing drill in Poland, looked intentional. Poland will ask NATO for more support on its eastern flank; NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte called the incident "clearly dangerous." Russia has not commented.
items.why: Russian weapons landing on NATO territory raises the risk of the war spilling into the alliance.

week.text: Anthropic's stock closed its first trading day about 17% above its $83 IPO price, but the wider market fell about 2% as AI shares slid.
week.detail: Anthropic opened at $111.50 shortly before noon, briefly valuing the company above $2 trillion and topping $115, before fading to close near $97. The S&P 500 erased an early 1.3% gain and fell about 2% for a sixth straight loss, its longest losing streak since April 2024; the Dow fell about 1,100 points (2.2%) to back below 50,000 and the Nasdaq lost about 2.3%. AMD dropped about 10% after investigative outlet Hunterbrook disclosed a short position citing its China dealings; AMD denied wrongdoing.
week.why: The record IPO was seen as a test of investor faith in AI, and it did not stop a weeks-long slide in tech stocks.

week.text: Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the U.N.'s top court ruled Thursday, the first time it has found a country itself responsible for genocide.
week.detail: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar's security forces intentionally killed Rohingya, caused them serious bodily or mental harm and imposed measures meant to prevent births during the 2017 "clearance operations" in northern Rakhine state, and that Myanmar failed to prevent and punish genocide. The court cited an estimated 10,000 Rohingya killed; about 700,000 fled to Bangladesh. It ordered Myanmar to investigate and prosecute those responsible, allow safe return of displaced Rohingya, and compensate them, with the amount to be set later; Myanmar must report back within two years. The judgment in the case brought by The Gambia in 2019 is final, binding and without appeal. U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres welcomed it.
week.why: It is the first time the world court has held a state directly responsible for committing genocide.

week.text: Measles is formally no longer eliminated in the U.S., Mexico and Bolivia, the Pan American Health Organization announced Tuesday, after a year of nonstop spread.
week.detail: PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa accepted the finding of the regional commission that met Nov. 10-13: the same measles strain circulated for 12 months or more in each country, with the U.S. reaching that mark on Jan. 20, 2026, Mexico on Feb. 1 and Bolivia on April 16. The U.S. had held elimination status for 26 years. The Americas have reported 58,213 confirmed cases and 82 deaths this year through Nov. 13, versus 12,806 cases a year earlier; the U.S. has more than 5,400 cases, its highest annual total since the 1989-91 resurgence, UNICEF said, 96% in unvaccinated people or those of unknown status. Canada lost its status in November 2025. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said the U.S. will work to regain the status and that he recommends the MMR vaccine.
week.why: It is official recognition that measles is again spreading continuously in the U.S.
